_meta.format: Every player-facing text value is an array of pages; each page fits 2 lines of 40 chars after word wrap ('\n' forces a break). Map spots are keyed maps.<map_id>.<spot_id>. Each spot has 'lines': an ordered list, most specific first, ending with id 'default' (flags [] and no 'when'). The engine shows the FIRST line whose 'flags' are all set (AND) and whose optional 'when' matches. 'pages' is kept as a mirror of the default line for older readers. battle_lost / battle_won / after / after_heal etc. are unchanged. Props: kind 'prop' (inspect) or 'trigger' (tile trigger); x,y = the cell the player faces, stand = where the player stands. Props/triggers: geometry (kind, x, y, stand, face, tile, trigger_when, opens, counter, states...) is copied from the map's interact_spots, which is the source of truth. Lines with no map spot live in top-level sections: company_inbox, ron_nicknames, ron_battle_openers, vane, catalogue, comfort, unplaced_npcs, unplaced (v0.4.2: text whose map spot is gone or not built yet), signs_awaiting_world_id. 'soul_item' = SOUL_PLAYBOOK item number (15:E# = easter egg). 'pending_story_call': true = neutral until Story Bot/Gary decide. 'story_ruling' = line follows a ruling in design/STORY_RULINGS_SOUL.md.

input_hints._note: Kilumen runs on PC (keyboard or controller, touch controls hidden) and on phones/tablets in landscape (touch: d-pad left; A, B, SEL right). Lines never name a key or a device; control placeholders resolve at runtime to a noun phrase for the CURRENT input device (last device used), so every line reads right on all three. Verbs in lines are device-neutral: 'Hold X to run', 'Use X to get on or off' (never press/click/tap). Source of current bindings: src/overworld/input.js (read-only).

contract.returns: noun phrase that completes 'Hold ___ to run.' / 'Use ___ to ...'

contract.prompt_glyph: when Coder's on-screen prompts land (battle/menu work), the runtime may swap the phrase for an inline glyph of the same control; ids below are the glyph ids, so text needs no change
contract.device_switch: re-resolve when the player switches device mid-page; never cache the phrase in the save

before: Survey in progress. East road's closed to unregistered trainers.
Bring me the Fernwick Master's coin. Yes, even if you work here.
after: You're registered now. Road east is open. Mind the bridge, it creaks.
Heading east? Drop this parcel at the Saltmere office. They'll pay you back.
after_parcel: Saltmere's past Aurelith. The parcel's not getting any lighter.

gives.name: Survey Parcel
received: {player} received the Survey Parcel! It's taped shut. Very shut.

before: A huge trunk lies across the trail. A Revival Tech notice is nailed to it.

REMOVAL SCHEDULED
Requests from two-coin trainers only.
after: Only sawdust is left where the trunk was.
Someone carved 'FINALLY' into the stump.

before: A wall of violet crystal hums across the path. It's warm to the touch.
Somewhere north, something is keeping it lit.
after: The crystals have gone dim and quiet. The way east is clear.

before: The rope bridge has snapped. Both halves are hanging off the cliffs.
Engineer: Repairs get approved when someone with three coins asks.
after: The bridge has been rebuilt. New rope, new planks.
Engineer: Rated for one person at a time. So, one person at a time.

before: The coast road is underwater. Deep enough to lose a boot. Maybe both.
prompt: The water's calm enough to cross. Use {skill}?
use: Hold on. It's faster than it looks.
cant_use_yet: A strong swimmer could carry you across, but you need {skill} first.
no_creature: The water's too deep to wade. None of your creatures knows {skill}.
after: You reach the far side. Mostly dry.

gate_cindervale_giant.species: TBD by Gary (no giant species in characters/NOTES.md yet)
before: A creature the size of a house is asleep on the road. It snores like a rockslide.
Pushing it does nothing. Yelling does nothing. It'll take something louder.
hint: Lanternport's lighthouse horn can be heard three towns over. Just saying.
wake: Far off, the Lanternport horn sounds. The giant opens one eye...
It gets up, grumbling, and lumbers off the road.
after: There's a giant dent in the road where it slept. The way to Cindervale is open.

gate_saltmere_causeway.role: flooded causeway (story, drains with the Frostspire thaw)
before: The causeway is under knee-deep meltwater. The far end is out of sight.
Local: Frostspire snowmelt. Drains when the thaw stops. Whenever that is.
after: The water's gone down. The causeway is muddy, but you can walk it.
Local: Told you. Smells like a pond that gave up, though.

before: Violet crystal spikes cover the slope. They hum like the Trail 1 wall.
There's no way down without shredding your boots. And your legs.
after: The crystals have gone dim and quiet. You can pick your way down to Sunmeadow.

gate_revival_checkpoint.role: Revival Tech security checkpoint (Heights south gate, opened from inside)
sign:
REVIVAL HEIGHTS SOUTH GATE
Residents and senior staff only.
before: Heights south gate. Residents and senior staff only.
Field staff come in through the Thornwood trail. Long way round, I know.
after: You beat the Heights Master? Fine. I'll open it from this side.
Saltmere's straight down the hill. Saves you the long way.
after_repeat: Gate's open for you now. Don't tell the other field staff.

gate_lanternport_tidelock.role: flooded tide-lock (shortcut home, opened from the Lanternport side)
gate_lanternport_tidelock.interaction: lock wheel (mechanism; not a field skill or item)
before: The tide-lock is shut. Seawater sits high against the gates.
The wheel that opens it is on the far side. Of course it is.
keeper_before: Lock stays shut till the Lanternport Master says so. Tides are no joke.
keeper_after: Our Master's coin? Then you can work the wheel. Turn it till it clunks.
use: You put your back into it. Clunk. The water drains out of the lock.
declined: You leave the wheel alone. The sea doesn't mind.
after: The tide-lock is open. Fernwick is a short walk east.

sign:
AURELITH ARENA
Challengers need all eight coins.
before: The doors are sealed. Eight empty coin slots run down the middle.
doorman_before: You've got {coins} coins. Come back with eight.
No, I can't make an exception. Nobody gets an exception.
doorman_after: Eight coins. Huh. Most people stop at five and blame the weather.
Go on in. Good luck. You'll need it.
after: The doors swing open. Eight Battle Masters are waiting inside.

entries._section: Kilindex blurbs (ui.T(blurbKey) from data/creatures_synced.json). One string, 2 lines x 40. DRAFT pending Gary. Validated by _kil_entries.

drizzlebill.blurb: Paddles the Brookhollow banks in the rain. Its bill hums before a storm.

mossmote.blurb: Lives in the moss on Trail 1 stones. Dries out, waits, wakes with the rain.

gladlet.blurb: Always smiling. Fernwick gardeners say any bed it naps in blooms early.

buoyling.blurb: Bobs about the harbour in its own float ring. Hugs anything that floats.

lumoris.blurb: Moves slowly and holds a glowfern close. Lost cavers follow its light out.

pandember.blurb: Its stripes glow like banked embers. It curls up warm on cold Thornwood nights.

vaultpede.blurb: Its plates lock shut like a vault door. Coils around Greystone's oldest stones.

pricklon.blurb: Up on four legs now. Its three-point crystal cluster hums when it's cross.

geodurchin.blurb: Each spire is a split geode, purple inside. Moss grows up its sides.

nibbin.blurb: The lab's earth partner. Gnaws tunnels in clay and brings back pebbles.

gnawford.blurb: Dams small streams with gnawed roots, then leaves a ford for anyone crossing.

jestrix.blurb: Rings its ear bell before every prank. Laughs loudest when it gets caught.

japkit.blurb: Juggles acorns, pebbles, anything. Drops the lot, except what it loves.

harlequop.blurb: Deals cards with a wink. Somehow the little ones always win the hand.

mummerhop.blurb: Twirls ribbons mid-battle. Every fight turns into a show, with encores.

maestrix.blurb: One ring of its bell and the meadow goes hush. It bows to friend and foe.

tbdcandle.blurb: Its flame burns pale blue in the cold. Drips little icicles, never wax.

parasoleaf.blurb: Opens its broad leaf when rain starts. Little creatures crowd under it.

drenchcrab.blurb: Comes out by the hundred when it rains. The road goes clickety for days.

reefshell.blurb: Swims the reef with little fish riding its shell. It never says no.

cliffpuff.blurb: Plunges off sea cliffs and comes up with a beakful of fish. Every time.

raywing.blurb: Leaps out of the water and glides a little way, just to see the sky.

lurelamp.blurb: Rises at night and lights whole patches of sea. Fish follow it home.

bristlereef.blurb: Spreads its spines wide to guard the reef. Small fish hide behind it.

wavelin.blurb: Rides the bow wave of every boat. Sailors call it good luck.

breakerfin.blurb: Leaps through breaking waves in perfect arcs. It scores itself.

spinyclaw.blurb: Clicks its antennae to chat with friends across the rock pools.

nudiblume.blurb: Looks like a flower, sways like a flower. Bees are always confused.

barnaclump.blurb: Sticks to ship hulls for free rides. It has seen every harbour.

foamkin.blurb: Pops into being on the crest of a wave. Gone again by the next one.

kelpstrider.blurb: Gallops across the waves on dim nights. Leaves no hoofprints.

hullwhale.blurb: Its songs cross the whole sea. Somewhere, another one sings back.

tidepony.blurb: Wraps its tail round the kelp and holds on through the strongest pull.

pearlisk.blurb: The pearl on its brow shows a different dream every night.

bleachghast.blurb: Drifts over pale reefs, hoping to bring their colours back.

squidge.blurb: Squirts water at anything that startles it. Then hides, embarrassed.

shorehound.blurb: Patrols the tide line every morning. Brings back whatever washed up.

_pending_r5_r6.helioseed: Turns its face to follow the sun all day. Sulks a bit at night.
_pending_r5_r6.heliobloom: Shares its seeds with every bird in the meadow. Birds adore it.
_pending_r5_r6.sunquail: Runs through tall grass in a neat line with its family. Nobody skips.
_pending_r5_r6.sunspeckle: Counts its spots every morning, just to be sure none went missing.
_pending_r5_r6.lopecalf: Follows anything that walks steadily. Farmers have to walk fast.
_pending_r5_r6.plainhorn: Grazes the uplands in big slow herds. Never in a hurry.
_pending_r5_r6.stampedor: When a herd of them runs, the ground drums for miles around.
_pending_r5_r6.popgopher: Pops up to say hello and is gone before you can answer.
_pending_r5_r6.thermalark: Sings higher than any other bird. Never lands mid-song.
_pending_r5_r6.sicklet: Bows politely before every battle. Then fights very hard.
_pending_r5_r6.reapmantis: Trims the meadow grass in neat patterns. Farmers leave it be.
_pending_r5_r6.basklet: Basks in the sun so long that its scales start to glow.
_pending_r5_r6.sunbasilisk: Spreads its frill to soak up heat by day, then glows all night.
_pending_r5_r6.dialmoss: Always knows the hour, even on cloudy days. Never late.
_pending_r5_r6.dewbell: Rings softly at dawn. Shares a sip of dew with tired travellers.
_pending_r5_r6.jestrix: Plays harmless tricks and laughs loudest when it gets caught.
_pending_r5_r6.aurelmare: Gallops across the uplands at sunrise. Its mane trails light.
_pending_r5_r6.glisterdew: Catches bugs on its sticky leaves, has a little chat, lets them go.
_pending_r5_r6.pollenub: Sneezes clouds of pollen whenever it laughs. It laughs a lot.
_pending_r5_r6.fenflick: Blinks on and off across the bog at night. Count them if you can.
_pending_r5_r6.bogbeacon: Leads travellers in circles until they laugh, then shows the way.
_pending_r5_r6.peatfrog: Croaks in chorus with a thousand others. It always starts.
_pending_r5_r6.peatbellow: Its croak rattles windows in the next town. It's very proud.
_pending_r5_r6.reedcrane: Dances in the dusk with its partner every spring.
_pending_r5_r6.bogsnout: Floats like a log and giggles when someone finds it.
_pending_r5_r6.mirejaw: Waits in the reed beds, patient as the bog itself.
_pending_r5_r6.fenmaw: Rules the deep pools. Even a grumpy Mirewump moves aside.
_pending_r5_r6.skimnymph: Skims the water in short hops. Never gets its feet wet.
_pending_r5_r6.bogdart: Darts over the bog faster than the eye can follow.
_pending_r5_r6.turfhulk: Sinks into the bog to sleep and rises again with the dusk.
_pending_r5_r6.murkgleam: Rolls over the boardwalks and hides them, just for fun.
_pending_r5_r6.pitchergulp: Slurps up rainwater and burps bubbles. No manners at all.
_pending_r5_r6.bulrusher: Builds reed houses and lets anyone who needs one move in.
_pending_r5_r6.mirewump: Lazy, grumpy, and very sure the whole bog belongs to it.
_pending_r5_r6.runeskein: When it is hurt, it unravels, then quietly weaves itself back.
_pending_r5_r6.mireglim: Hides in hollow logs and giggles at anyone walking past.
_pending_r5_r6.gloommire: Brings the dark in at dusk and carries it off again at dawn.
_pending_r5_r6.glimmoth: Only flies when the dusk is thick. Its wings glow faintly.
_pending_r5_r6.kneeroot: Sticks up out of the water and pretends to be a stump. Badly.
_pending_r5_r6.cypresshade: Shades the bog on hot days. Everything rests under it.
_pending_r5_r6.silteel: Wriggles under the boardwalks and tickles bare feet.
_pending_r5_r6.duckmoss: Paddles the bog, mistaken for a floating patch of green.
_pending_r5_r6.mudwhisk: Knows every hidden pool in the bog. Tells nobody.
_pending_r5_r6.sprinkit: Shakes the rain off all over its friends. On purpose.
_pending_r5_r6.downpaw: Runs along flooded roads, splashing as hard as it can.
_pending_r5_r6.deluvane: Walks ahead of the storms. Farmers cheer for it in dry years.
_pending_r5_r6.petrelet: Patters across puddles as if it could walk on water.
_pending_r5_r6.galepetrel: Flies into storms, never away from them.
_pending_r5_r6.slurrymole: Digs tunnels that fill with rain for others to swim in.
_pending_r5_r6.brinehopper: Hops along the flood line after a storm, seeing what's new.
_pending_r5_r6.surfskipper: Skips over the waves like a flat stone. Never sinks.
_pending_r5_r6.driftknot: Washes ashore after each storm, somewhere new every time.
_pending_r5_r6.reefhatch: Races to the sea under the moon the night it hatches.
_pending_r5_r6.atollback: Sailors once mistook a sleeping one for an island. It didn't mind.
_pending_r5_r6.puffling: Waddles to the cliff edge and has a good long think.
_pending_r5_r6.mantlet: Flaps along the sea floor, stirring up little clouds of sand.
_pending_r5_r6.abyssray: Glides over the deep reef like the shadow of a cloud.
_pending_r5_r6.anglet: Small, hungry, and very proud of its little lure.
_pending_r5_r6.spinurch: Rolls slowly over the reef, nibbling algae as it goes.
_pending_r5_r6.sandpup: Digs a hole in the beach, lies in it, and naps till high tide.
_pending_r5_r6.divegannet: Drops like an arrow from great heights. Barely a splash.
_pending_r5_r6.shellsinger: Sings with the tide, and the sea sings back.

system_company_voice._section: Company voice (Gary Oct 23 2026, 12:19-12:22 PM CT). Default on from v0.2.0-alpha (Gary 1:00 PM CT Oct 23), region 1 events only. Sarcastic company AI RITA (Resource Inventory and Tracking Assistant) that only cares about company asset value; always addresses the player by bare {employee_id}, never praises them as a person. Structure only from Satisfactory; no names or lines copied. Read by src/systems/company_voice.js. DRAFT Oct 23 2026 12:35 PM CT. RITA whole-game pass (Text Bot, Oct 23 2026 ~12:45 PM CT; Gary 12:33-12:34 PM CT: realistic milestones, lines for the whole game). region = first region where the line can fire (region n = after Master n-1 up to beating Master n; 9 = after Master 8: finale + postgame; Kilindex counts: first region whose cumulative obtainable species reach the count). Kilindex counts now 10, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400, 450 (Coder: add 200, 300, 400 to data/company_voice.json kilindex_milestone.counts). Optional specific sets (Coder: look up <line>_<ctx.key> first, then the generic line): master_beaten_<flag key> (beat_master_<key>: fernwick, saltmere, revival, frostspire, mirefen, tidewater, lanternport, cindervale), rival_beaten_ron_<n> (beat_rival_ron_<n>; 'ron_' so it never reads as variant _2/_3/_4), area_new_<map id>, quest_done_<quest id> (q_<id>_done). Higher rank, higher targets. You'll love it.

Touch only what you can log.

Assets are not waterproof. Please keep them dry.

pages: Station M Key Card
RT key card. Opens Mirefen Peat Station, under the bog.
Do not bend. Do not lose. It is billed.
Station T Key Card
RT key card. Opens the Tidewater Signal Lab in the sea cave.
Salt-proof, it says. Nobody tested that.
You got the {item}!
A little light on it blinks green. It knows who you are.
A heavy RT door. The card reader blinks red.
STAFF WITH RESEARCH ACCESS ONLY.
The reader blinks green. The door hisses open.
Cold air. Old paper. Something moves inside.
Ron squints at the reader.
'They gave us IDs, not keys. Classic.'

RT MIREFEN PEAT STATION
Lumen yield survey. Wipe your feet.
Research-only creatures inside. Logs required.
A swollen notebook. 'Day 40. Bog lights again.
They walk us in circles, then laugh. Bogbeacon.'
A clipboard. 'Herd ran overhead all night.
The tanks rattled. Stampedor. Writing that down.'
A note taped to a tank: 'DO NOT knock on glass.
The Fenmaw doesn't like it. Neither do I.'
The last page is water-stained.
'Lights off at dusk. Gloommire likes the dark.'

RT TIDEWATER SIGNAL LAB
Open at low tide only.
Research-only creatures inside. Logs required.
A pinned chart. 'A shadow on the reef again.
Not a cloud. Abyssray. It glides right under us.'
A logbook. 'Lights in the pools at night.
Lurelamps, dozens. Like the sea is breathing.'
A sticky note: 'Pearlisk showed me a dream.
My old house. I didn't know I missed it.'
Scrawled on the wall: 'THE ISLAND MOVED.'
Under it, smaller: 'Atollback. Sorry. Noted.'
These creatures live nowhere else.
They're tougher, and harder to catch. Take your time.
Promotion review: log three research-only kinds
at Mirefen Peat Station. Then report to the outpost.
Promotion filed. New title: Wetland Field Lead.
Your desk is still a bog. Well done, we suppose.
Promotion review: log three research-only kinds
at the Tidewater Signal Lab. Then report in.
Promotion filed. Title: Coastal Operations Lead.
The title comes with a towel. Not a pay rise.

STORM SEASON
The sky over the coast goes dark.
Roads near the sea may flood. Some won't drain.
